commit.message:
[TECHOPS-1265] Move the four remaining release jobs onto the release-scoped vault role (#8019)

* [TECHOPS-1265] Move the four remaining release jobs onto the release-scoped vault role

Four jobs on this repository's release path still assumed
`liquibase-vault-oidc-role`, whose GitHub trust matches any repository in the
liquibase, Datical and datical orgs. Between them they read two GPG keys, the
Install4j licence, the DigiCert KeyLocker family and the GitHub App key, and two
of them run on a public repository.

Three of the four already declared `release` or `release-publish`, which is the
entire trust on `liquibase-release-vault-oidc-role`, so they were pointing at the
wrong role rather than missing a gate: those are a one-line change each and need
no infrastructure work. `update-dockerfiles` in docker-release.yml declared no
environment, so it takes the same `approved` input the other publishing callees
use before it can move.

- create-release.yml: `reversion`, `build-installers` and `tag-release` assume
  the release-scoped role
- docker-release.yml: `update-dockerfiles` gains the workflow_call-only
  `approved` input and the environment expression, then the same role swap
- release-published-orchestrator.yml: `release-docker` passes `approved: true`,
  so an orchestrated release costs no extra approval
- README: the per-job role table had drifted. javadocs and publish-assets-s3
  moved to /vault/devops in TECHOPS-1320, the second-hop role chain now exists
  only in build-logic, and the release role's tag subjects are gone.

The remaining broad-role holder on this path is `package`, in build-logic's
shared package.yml, which needs its own change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Trim the new comments to one sentence each

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [TECHOPS-1265] Mark release-docker broad and warn that approved stays workflow_call-only

Review follow-ups:
- release-docker's two image builds run build-logic's reusable-docker-build.yml,
  which still assumes the broad vault role, loads /vault/liquibase whole and
  chains AWS_PROD_GITHUB_OIDC_ROLE_ARN_INFRASTRUCTURE, so the role table and the
  flowchart now mark it broad and the blast-radius paragraph lists it next to
  package.yml.
- docker-release.yml gets the same warning as the other publishing callees:
  adding approved to workflow_dispatch would let anyone who can dispatch skip
  the reviewers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(release): publish OSS released assets to their own R2 bucket (TECHOPS-1320) (#8018)

#8005 published to s3://liquibase-org-assets/oss-released-assets/, but the
infrastructure side deliberately created a separate bucket for them. From
cloudflare/storage.tf:

  separate bucket for oss-released-assets/ ... R2 custom domains and public
  access are bucket-scoped, not prefix-scoped, so sharing a bucket would force
  this Access-gated bucket to also be public.

The split never reached this workflow, and liquibase-oss-released-assets is
currently referenced by no publisher at all.

This matters more than a wrong path usually would. liquibase-org-assets carries
an R2 bucket lock with Indefinite retention, so anything written there is
immutable and undeletable. Publishing release artifacts into it would make them
permanently undeletable, put them behind the compliance bucket's Access gate,
and leave no way to build the public consumption path the separate bucket
exists for, short of making the compliance bucket public.

Caught before the S3 to R2 migration ran, so nothing has landed in the locked
bucket yet.

The oss-released-assets/ key prefix is kept inside the new bucket rather than
flattened to the root, so the migration stays a 1:1 copy of the S3 layout.
Consumption is still a follow-up, so that can be changed cheaply if a flat
layout is preferred.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message: chore(release): stop double-writing XSDs to liquibaseorg-origin S3 [TECHOPS-1320] (#8006) * chore(release): stop double-writing XSDs to liquibaseorg-origin S3 release-deploy-xsd.yml already SFTPs the same xml/ns/dbchangelog files to WPEngine right after syncing them to s3://liquibaseorg-origin, and WPEngine (not S3) is what serves customer XSD/JSON schema reads. The S3 bucket is not publicly readable, so the S3 write had no reader. Remove the S3 upload and the S3-backed index.htm bookkeeping instead of migrating them to R2. index.htm is now fetched straight from WPEngine over SFTP, edited, and pushed back the same way, dropping the dead round trip through S3. This also drops the now-unused prod build-logic AWS role assumption from this job, a privilege reduction. TECHOPS-1320 * fix(security): validate inputs.version before shell interpolation in release-deploy-xsd (TECHOPS-1320) Pass inputs.version through env and read it as $VERSION instead of interpolating the raw expression into the script, then require the major and minor components to be numeric before building xsd_version. Closes the CWE-78 command injection path CodeRabbit flagged, without rejecting the release-candidate or hotfix tag suffixes this repo actually uses (e.g. 5.0.0-RC1, 4.25.1-release). Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 * fix: harden index.htm SFTP fetch and match full XSD filename in release-deploy-xsd (TECHOPS-1320) Run the index.htm download in sftp batch mode (-b -) under set -euo pipefail so a failed or partial get aborts this step instead of exiting 0, which previously let a truncated file reach the unconditional SFTP upload step that follows and overwrite the live index. Add explicit non-empty and -marker checks on the download as defense in depth on top of that. Also match the complete "dbchangelog-X.Y.xsd" filename instead of a bare version substring: the substring check treated dbchangelog-4.20.xsd as proof that 4.2 already existed, so a 4.2.x release would skip adding its own index entry. Verified against 4.1 vs 4.10-4.19 and 4.2 vs 4.20, no false-positive matches remain. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 * chore(release): condense release-deploy-xsd comments (TECHOPS-1320) Trim the S3-removal and SFTP-hardening comments to what stays true after merge: the batch-mode/exit-code reasoning for -b -, the exact filename match, and short ticket references. Evidence and the S3 removal rationale already live in the PR description. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5

commit.message:
chore(release): publish OSS released assets to R2 instead of S3 [TECHOPS-1320] (#8005)

* chore(release): publish OSS released assets to R2 instead of S3

liquibaseorg-origin is being decommissioned (TECHOPS-969). Point the
oss-released-assets publish step at the Cloudflare R2 bucket
liquibase-org-assets instead, preserving the oss-released-assets/
prefix. The prod-account S3 write role is no longer needed for this
job, so the credential chain now loads only the R2 S3-API creds from
/vault/devops, matching the pattern already used by build-logic's
package.yml and liquibase-pro's publish-to-s3.yml.

Refs TECHOPS-1320, TECHOPS-969

* fix(security): restore hardened TECHOPS-1107 vault reader in release-publish-assets-s3 (TECHOPS-1320)

Port the TECHOPS-1107 vault-reader pattern back into this workflow's
Cloudflare R2 credential read instead of the naive jq -r version: the
jq -j plus printf sentinel that preserves a value's real trailing
newline, mask-escaping % before \r and \n so add-mask actually matches
what the runner unescapes, and a random heredoc delimiter into
GITHUB_ENV instead of k=v so a newline in a secret cannot inject
arbitrary GITHUB_ENV entries. Only the secret id and key list differ
from the release-deploy-xsd.yml original.

Also fix the deployment-pipeline diagram in README.md: it still
classified publish-assets-s3 as :::scoped after the table above it was
already updated to broad, contradicting this PR's own documentation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(release): condense the R2 vault-reader comments (TECHOPS-1320)

Trim the credential-loading and upload comments to the technical
constraints that stay true after merge: the jq sentinel, the mask
escape order, the session-token drop, and the CRC32 checksum override.
Ticket history, bucket names and cross-repo pattern notes already live
in the PR description.

commit.message:
feat(javadocs): publish javadocs to Cloudflare R2 as well as S3 (TECHOPS-1318) (#8004)

* feat(javadocs): publish javadocs to Cloudflare R2 as well as S3 (TECHOPS-1318)

javadocs.liquibase.com is served from Cloudflare R2, but this workflow only ever
wrote to the S3 origin. The one thing carrying those files across was Sippy, a
lazy copy-on-first-read bridge that liquibase-infrastructure#4391 removes. With
Sippy gone and no R2 write here, the next release would land in S3 and never
reach the edge, freezing the published javadocs silently until someone noticed.
That is the TECHOPS-805 failure mode the Wave 3 epic exists to unwind.

Adds an R2 sync alongside the existing S3 one, reusing the pattern already proven
in liquibase-pro publish-to-s3.yml: load CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and the R2 S3-API
key pair from the devops vault via the org-level DEVOPS_VAULT_OIDC_ROLE_ARN,
pulling only those three keys and masking them rather than importing the vault.

Two details that are easy to get wrong against R2:
  * env -u AWS_SESSION_TOKEN - the step runs under an assumed role, and R2 does
    not recognise that session token, so SigV4 fails if it is left set.
  * --checksum-algorithm CRC32 - the newer AWS CLI default checksum trailer is
    not supported by R2.

S3 is kept deliberately. The origin bucket retires on its own ticket
(TECHOPS-876), and writing both means javadocs publish correctly whether or not
the Sippy removal has applied yet. Drop the S3 line with the bucket.

Measured before this change: the S3 origin held 3,673 objects against 3,265 in
R2, so 408 had never been lazily copied - whole trees including
liquibase-maven-plugin, liquibase-cdi-jakarta, liquibase-cdi and liquibase-cli. A
Super Slurper pass has since closed that gap; this change keeps it closed.

* fix(javadocs): make the R2 publish non-fatal and keep it clear of the S3 path (TECHOPS-1318)

Strict review found the first version introduced a regression with a much wider
blast radius than the problem it solved.

The R2 credential steps sat ahead of the S3 sync, so any hard failure in them - a
rotated /vault/devops key, an unassumable devops role - exited the job before
javadocs reached S3 at all, a path that works today. Worse,
release-published-orchestrator.yml gates deploy-maven on this job's result
(needs.deploy-javadocs.result == 'success' || 'skipped'), so a red javadocs job
SKIPS the Maven Central deployment for that release, and the orchestrator's final
check_stage marks the whole release failed.

Restructured so the existing path cannot regress:
  * Steps 1-5 are byte-identical to main. The S3 sync carries no continue-on-error
    and no if:, so its behaviour is unchanged.
  * All three R2 steps now come AFTER it and are continue-on-error, each gated on
    the previous one succeeding.
  * A broken R2 leg degrades to stale javadocs plus a ::warning::, never a failed
    release.

Also from the same review: the credential-loading step now mirrors the escaping
the existing vault step in this file deliberately uses. That step's own comment
explains why - the runner unescapes %0D, %0A and %25 in command data, so a value
carrying those literals registers a mask that never matches it. The first version
used the simpler form from publish-to-s3.yml and lost that hardening.

The pre-flight credential guard also moved ahead of the write it guards, instead
of sitting after it.

* fix(javadocs): let the warn step see a failed R2 sync (TECHOPS-1318)

Review by sayaliM0412 on PR #8004, same finding from coderabbitai.

The publish step is continue-on-error and had no id, so the warn step could
only ever catch credential problems. When the sync itself fails, from a wrong
bucket, a SigV4 rejection, an R2 5xx or a token scope, both r2-auth and
r2-creds are still success, the warn step is skipped, and the job reports green
with javadocs in S3 only. That is exactly the TECHOPS-805 failure mode this PR
exists to prevent, and it matters because liquibase-infrastructure#4391 removes
Sippy on the strength of this workflow working.

continue-on-error rewrites a step's conclusion to success but leaves its
outcome as failure, so reading the real result needs an id. Adds id:
r2-publish and includes its outcome in the condition. A skipped publish also

wrote to the S3 origin. The one thing carrying those files across was Sippy, a

    not recognise that session token, so SigV4 fails if it is left set.

    not supported by R2.

the Sippy removal has applied yet. Drop the S3 line with the bucket.

fix(ci): let a dispatched dry run pass the green-SHA gate (TECHOPS-929) (#8015)

* fix(ci): let a dispatched dry run pass the green-SHA gate (TECHOPS-929)

dry-run-release.yml dispatches create-release.yml and waits on it, so the
caller is always in flight on the same head_sha the gate judges. On the weekly
schedule that run is dropped by the gate's event != schedule filter, so nobody
noticed. Trigger the dry run by hand and nothing drops it, the gate reports

  <sha> still has workflows running: Dry run release

and the dispatch can never succeed. workflow_dispatch of dry-run-release.yml
was therefore permanently broken while the scheduled path stayed green.

This is the same failure the gate already documents for SELF, one level up.
The caller now names itself via a new optional caller_workflow input and is
excluded on the same grounds: the workflow driving this release attempt is not
evidence about whether the commit builds. The input defaults to empty and
.name != "" excludes nothing, so a direct dispatch of create-release is
unchanged.

Found while unblocking TECHOPS-929, which needs an on-demand dry run to verify
publishing to the R2 bucket rather than waiting for the weekly schedule.

fix(docker): match the zlib rule on fields Grype populates (TECHOPS-929) (#8014)

The rule added in #8013 matched nothing. It keyed on fix-state: not-fixed, but
Grype emits fix: {"versions": [], "state": ""} for this finding, an empty
state rather than not-fixed, because no advisory exists to describe a fix state

actually set: any other zlib version stops matching and the scan goes red.

The mechanism from liquibase/build-logic#710 is confirmed working: the
"Fetch caller .grype.yaml" step ran and succeeded, so only the rule was wrong.

feat(docker): add community Grype ignore rules with the zlib no-fix entry (TECHOPS-929) (#8013)

The community counterpart to liquibase-pro vex/assessments.yaml, which covers
Liquibase Secure only. docker/.trivyignore suppresses Trivy findings; this
suppresses Grype findings. Both are needed because Trivy reads the distro
security database and Grype reads upstream advisories, so they disagree when a
distro has not issued an advisory yet.

Wired up by liquibase/build-logic#710.

First rule is CVE-2026-85091 in zlib 1.3.2-r0, which has kept the Docker
workflow red on main since 2026-09-21 and therefore blocks create-release's
green-SHA gate, the weekly dry run, and any real release.

It is not a not-affected claim. Alpine has published no advisory and no fixed
zlib, and Dockerfile.alpine already runs apk upgrade, so no remediation exists
to apply. The rule is scoped to fix-state not-fixed so it expires by itself the
moment a fixed package ships.

commit.message:
[TECHOPS-1307] Create the Jira ticket from the merge commit, not the fork PR event (#8003)

This workflow exists to guarantee a SECURE Story for every merged Community
PR. It never worked for the contributions it was built for.

It triggered on `pull_request: closed` and needs `id-token: write` to assume
the vault OIDC role and read the Jira service-account credentials. GitHub
does not grant that permission on a `pull_request` event raised by a fork:
the token is read-only and no secrets are exposed. The job failed before it
reached Jira, so every merged external PR silently got no ticket. 32 of the
workflow's 34 recorded failures have a fork head repository, against 2 from
liquibase/liquibase. The last merged fork PR was #7909 on 2026-08-14, and it
failed; none has been merged since, which is why nobody noticed.

React to the merge landing on main instead. A push to a protected branch is
trusted code and does carry secrets. Squash is the only merge strategy
enabled here, so one pushed commit maps to exactly one merged PR.

`pull_request_target` would have fixed this too, and would have been safe
because this workflow never checks out PR code. It is deliberately not used:
TECHOPS-1100 left this repository with zero pull_request_target files, and
that absolute is what makes the fork policy auditable with one grep.

Also:
- The `pull_request: milestoned` arm stays for the forgot-the-milestone case
  but is now restricted to PRs whose head is this repository, so a fork PR
  reaching it reports nothing instead of failing red.
- Adds `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr_number` input to backfill the PRs
  already missed. The value is passed through the environment and validated
  as digits in the script, never interpolated into a shell command.
- Commit-to-PR association is not immediately consistent, so an empty answer
  falls back to the `(#1234)` suffix of the squash subject. Verified against
  the last 12 subjects on main: 12/12.
- Declares `issues: read`. The milestone-rename handler reads PRs through
  issues.listForRepo, which that scope gates and `pull-requests` does not.

enabled here, so one pushed commit maps to exactly one merged PR.

`pull_request_target` would have fixed this too, and would have been safe
because this workflow never checks out PR code. It is deliberately not used:
TECHOPS-1100 left this repository with zero pull_request_target files, and
that absolute is what makes the fork policy auditable with one grep.

Also:
- The `pull_request: milestoned` arm stays for the forgot-the-milestone case
  but is now restricted to PRs whose head is this repository, so a fork PR
  reaching it reports nothing instead of failing red.
- Adds `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr_number` input to backfill the PRs
  already missed. The value is passed through the environment and validated
  as digits in the script, never interpolated into a shell command.
- Commit-to-PR association is not immediately consistent, so an empty answer
  falls back to the `(#1234)` suffix of the squash subject. Verified against
  the last 12 subjects on main: 12/12.
- Declares `issues: read`. The milestone-rename handler reads PRs through
  issues.listForRepo, which that scope gates and `pull-requests` does not.

[TECHOPS-1223] Stop the release green-check gate counting its own runs (#8000)

create-release.yml is named 'Attach Artifacts To Draft Release' and is dispatched with --ref main and branch: main, so its own run carried the head_sha it was judging. In flight it read as 'still running'; after failing it read as a failing workflow, which poisoned that commit permanently. Excludes its own name via github.workflow.

commit.message:
[TECHOPS-1264] Document how a release goes and which guards need a person (#7986)

* [TECHOPS-1264] Document how a release goes and which guards need a person

The README already says what each release workflow does, and which role and
secrets each job reaches. Two things it never said:

1. **What a release feels like to run.** There was no plain-language account of
   the sequence, so the fact that only two moments need a person, and that one
   approval covers the whole release, was only inferable by reading the
   `needs:` graph and the environment expression. Adds a five-step table and
   states the per-job-not-per-run approval behaviour that the two-environment
   split exists to work around.

2. **The guards as a list.** The existing table is organised per job, which
   answers "what does this job reach" but not "what stops a bad release".
   Adds a per-guard table with a Person/Automatic column, and points at the
   per-job table for the detail rather than repeating it.

Also documents the `refs/tags/v*` tag ruleset, which is live but appeared
nowhere in this repository, including that it is at `enforcement = "evaluate"`
and therefore records rather than blocks.

Calls out that `needs: manual-approval` is load-bearing on its own: since the
publishing jobs no longer sit behind reviewers themselves, that edge is the only
thing keeping the gate in front of them, and removing it would not show up as a
change to any environment or any infrastructure code.

Documentation only, no workflow touched. `:traffic_light:` rather than
`:shield:` on the new heading because a `:shield:` section already exists.
Tables checked for consistent column counts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [TECHOPS-1264] Correct the person count and the role-trust claim in the release docs

Review follow-ups on the new sections:

- The walkthrough said two moments need a person while its own table marked
  three (start create-release.yml, publish the draft, approve). Says three, and
  the guards section notes why only two of them are guards.
- The role-trust row claimed the trust stops any job that declares no
  environment. It does not: vault-manager/liquibase-release-oidc-role.tf:63-64
  on liquibase-infrastructure main still lists
  repo:liquibase/liquibase:ref:refs/tags/v* and its immutable-subject twin, and
  every release: published run is on a v* tag, so a job with no environment
  would be trusted. Row now says what the trust does stop, and that all four
  jobs reading the role declare an environment, so those subjects can come out.
- The guards intro said the automatic guards "hold whether anyone is watching
  or not", which is not true of the refs/tags/v* ruleset at enforcement =
  "evaluate". It now points at the two rows that do not hold on their own.

Verified: no ragged tables; no workflow in this repo triggers on tag push, so
the reachable v* subject is a release: published run or a dispatch against a
tag; all four release-scoped-role callees declare
environment: ${{ inputs.approved && 'release-publish' || 'release' }}.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
[TECHOPS-1214] Push the release tag with the liquibase-workflows app token (#7985)

* [TECHOPS-1214] Push the release tag with the liquibase-workflows app token

A repository ruleset cannot grant a bypass to GITHUB_TOKEN. Its app is
GitHub's own global `github-actions` app (id 15368, owner `github`), which is
not an org installation, so GitHub rejects it as a bypass actor:

    422 Validation Failed
    Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or
    owner organization

That is what failed the first apply of the `refs/tags/v*` ruleset in
liquibase-infrastructure. The tag namespace cannot be restricted while the
release tag is pushed by an identity that can never hold a bypass, so the push
moves to `liquibase-workflows` (LIQUIBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID), which is installed in
the org and is already a bypass actor on strict_branch_protection and
strict_status_checks.

- The vault read in `reversion` now also loads the app id and private key,
  reusing the masking loop already there.
- The token requests `permission-contents: write` only, which is all a tag push
  needs, and is minted under the same `if:` as the push so a dry run or a
  standalone-zip run mints nothing.
- The push uses an explicit `x-access-token` URL rather than a named remote, so
  the token never reaches `.git/config`. `-c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=`
  clears the basic-auth header actions/checkout leaves behind, which otherwise
  takes precedence over URL credentials.
- `persist-credentials` drops to false. Nothing else in this job touches git, so
  the job no longer carries a push-capable GITHUB_TOKEN it does not use.

Verified: `actionlint` reports the same 34 findings as main, none new, and the
file still parses. LIQUIBASE_GITHUB_APP_ID in /vault/liquibase is 1241802,
matching the `liquibase-workflows` installation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [TECHOPS-1214] Scope the app token to this repo and keep its key out of the job env

Review follow-ups on the tag-push token:

- The liquibase-workflows installation (65890526) is repository_selection:
  all, so `owner` with no `repositories` minted a contents:write token over
  every repo in the org. Scoped to the repo the tag is pushed to.
- The vault loop wrote every key to GITHUB_ENV, so the app private key was in
  the environment of every later step, including "Re-version Artifacts", which
  curls three scripts and executes them. The two app keys now go to the step's
  outputs, which only the token step reads; the rest are unchanged.
- Dropped `-c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=`. actions/checkout calls
  removeAuth() whenever persist-credentials is false, so there was no header
  left to clear and the comment's reason was wrong.

Verified: actionlint reports the same 34 findings as main and none new;
shellcheck is clean on the rewritten step; replaying the loop against a
fixture puts the app id and PEM in GITHUB_OUTPUT only, leaves the PEM out of
GITHUB_ENV, and preserves the PEM's trailing newline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
[TECHOPS-1099] Remove the release-docker.yml pass-through and dead owasp block (#7972)

release-docker.yml existed only to call docker-release.yml. It renamed two
inputs (version -> liquibaseVersion, dry_run -> dryRun), re-declared the same
three permissions, and passed nothing else. Its single caller, the release
orchestrator, now calls docker-release.yml directly.

Nothing is lost by removing it. docker-release.yml already exposes both
workflow_call and workflow_dispatch, so the manual entry point survives, and
the orchestrator's job-level permissions block is what applied to the called
workflow either way. The orchestrator's job is still named release-docker, so
its needs graph and run summary are untouched.

Two documentation errors fixed while in there. The workflows README described
this step under the wrapper's old input names, and claimed "This triggers a
workflow in the liquibase/docker repository". docker-release.yml has no
reference to liquibase/docker; the images are built in this repository. Someone
following that note during a failed release would have gone looking in the
wrong repo.

Also strips the commented-out owasp-scanner job from create-release.yml.
owasp-scanner.yml was retired under TECHOPS-1112, so the block cannot be
uncommented into anything that exists.

Verified: actionlint finding profile identical to main for both changed
workflows (36 findings before and after), YAML parses, and the orchestrator's
uses: path resolves to a file that is present.
